chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban, from Ibn Mudarib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever accuses his wife before he consummates the marriage with her, he is whipped the Hadd penalty, and she remains his wife.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling if a husband accuses his wife of adultery before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies a specific legal nuance in Shia jurisprudence: while the husband incurs the Hadd punishment for slander (qadhf) against his wife prior to consummation, the marriage contract (nikah) remains valid and is not annulled. This ruling distinguishes the penal consequence from the civil status of the union, ensuring the wife retains her marital rights despite the accusation.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban, from Ibn Muzarab, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘The one who accuses his wife before he copulates with her would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd), and she would (still) be his wife’.
